speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: asked the Minister for Manpower (a) which are the top five industries that freelancers are venturing into; and (b) whether more grants and mentorship programmes will be given to support freelancers outside of the creative industry.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: We encourage all workers, including SEPs, to take advantage of such schemes to upgrade and improve skills and competencies continuously.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: The Second Minister mentioned there are schemes to help them.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: How well are these schemes currently taken up?

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: I understand that this group is also not a permanent group; they are a transient group.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: Some of them will be freelancers for a while, and then they will find a full-time job, and then they may go back again.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: The issue now is how to help them to continue to upskill.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: We are also worried about them being stagnant in one position and miss out the entire innovativeness of the economy as the economy improves.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: Can the Second Minister update us as to how much the freelancers in these five industries utilise the schemes she just mentioned?

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I will be talking about this during the Committee of Supply debate for the Ministry of Manpower.
